issues.description: HAS_NUMERIC regex misses 'lighter'/'bolder' edge and over-matches numeric substrings in named context
issues.detail: `\b(?:100|200|...|900)\b` will match any 3-digit token boundary, including inside calc()/var() fallbacks or custom-ident-like values that contain those digits as standalone tokens. Low-impact since it only widens to the slow path, but the asymmetry with HAS_NAMED (case-insensitive) versus HAS_NUMERIC (case-sensitive) is inconsistent and undocumented. Pick one stance.

issues.description: import-notation early-return ignores case beyond `url(` and skips comments/whitespace before the token
issues.detail: `/url\(/i.test(params)` is a decent prefilter, but `primary === 'url'` returns when ANY `url(` appears in params — that is exactly what we want to skip for the URL form, fine. However, the `string` branch returns when `url(` is absent, which is correct. Just verify `params` never contains a string literal containing `url(` as text; if it does, you bail to slow path, which is safe. Acceptable. Minor: extract the regex to a const to match the pattern used in sibling files.

issues.description: keyframe-selector-notation: HAS_PERCENTAGE lacks case-insensitive flag while HAS_KEYWORD has it
issues.detail: Percentage selectors like `0%`, `100%` are digits so case doesn't matter — fine. But the regex `(?:^|[,\s])(?:0%|...)` is anchored to comma/whitespace/start; a selector like `from,100%` works, `from ,100%` works. Confirm selectors that are valid CSS but use unusual whitespace (tabs, newlines inside `@keyframes` rule selectors) still match — `\s` covers it. Acceptable but worth a test.

issues.description: `selectorRegex = /./` as a sentinel is bad taste
issues.detail: The walkRules filter accepts a regex; using `/./` to mean 'match everything' is clever-where-it-could-be-obvious. Cleaner: branch on whether a filter exists and call `walkRules(filter, cb)` or `walkRules(cb)`. Same machine code, readable diff for the next maintainer. Special case eliminated.

issues.description: selector-pseudo-element-colon-notation: `/:/` filter matches pseudo-classes too, no perf win for selector-heavy sheets
issues.detail: The old code did `selector.includes(':')` then proceeded — identical semantics. Moving it into the walk filter is consistent with the stated goal but doesn't reduce work for selectors containing any `:`. That's fine and matches the PR's stated intent (consistency with other selector-* rules). Just note: the perf benefit here is marginal compared to the other rules in this patch.

issues.description: Six rules touched in one changeset — THREE-PATCHES territory
issues.detail: Each rule's prefilter has its own correctness surface (font-weight regex construction, import-notation url detection, keyframe selector filter, media-feature range tokens, two selector-* moves). Landing as one is acceptable since they share a theme and a single changeset entry, but if any one regresses, bisecting becomes annoying. Acceptable for this codebase's conventions; flagging as taste, not blocker.

review.summary: The patch does one thing well: add cheap prefilters before expensive parser walks across six `*-notation` rules. The diffs are small, scoped, and match the surrounding voice. Taste issues are minor: `/./` as a "match everything" sentinel in keyframe-selector-notation is the kind of clever-instead-of-obvious choice the next maintainer will frown at, and the case-sensitivity asymmetry between HAS_NAMED and HAS_NUMERIC in font-weight-notation deserves a comment. The perf claim is plausible — regex test on `decl.value` or `atRule.params` is orders of magnitude faster than valueParser + selector parse for the common no-op case. NEEDS-WORK on the `/./` sentinel; otherwise lands.
